text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- About every Norwegian above 12 years of age watched television seven minutes longer in 1996 than in 1995. The daily average for TV watching is two and a half hour.

- In May 1995, teenager Birgitte Tengs was raped and killed near her home in Haugesund on the west coast in a murder that shocked Norway. After the most extensive investigation for years, police now have arrested a suspect, a 19-year-old relative of the victim.

- Some 1.2 million Norwegians receive social welfare contributions. The Social Welfare Authority's expenses increased by five percent in 1996. Dagfinn Hoybraaten, social welfare manager, says the increase is too high.
- In an analysis of the strong Norwegian economy, the IMF is warning the country against allowing too high wage increases in 1997.
- Norwegian exports to France increased by 35 percent in 1996.
- Prices increased by three percent from January 1996 to January 1997. Handelsbanken chief economist Knut Anton Mork says he is surprised that the inflation is so high already.
